element: Domain 2 skill-area structure (2.1-2.7 organized by technology family)
rationale: Seven skill areas are technology families (GIS, data management, field technology, analytics, collaboration tools, AI monitoring, immersive tech). About 9 of 35 competencies are almost pure tool fluency (2.3.4, 2.3.5, 2.5.1, 2.5.3, 2.7.1, 2.7.2, 2.7.4 retire; 2.1.3, 2.3.2 largely). Reorganize data craft by durable function along the information chain: Acquire (monitoring/measurement design, field data capture, sensor data engineering), Steward (data management, QC, provenance, publication, sensitive data), Analyze & Model (statistics, spatial, RS, ML/foundation models, process models, forecast systems), Integrate & Communicate (decision support, visual evidence, uncertainty, LLM text analysis), Assure & Govern (AI validation, HITL design, evaluation sets, model risk, procurement, enterprise governance). Tools move to a separate layer (tools_layer_proposal.csv).

Advanced/Expert statements are generic and unobservable across nearly all 35 competencies ('Shapes GIS strategy and standards', 'Provides leadership on ...', 'Expert in ...'). They cannot support hiring or assessment (IO's standard). Replace with scope-of-accountability anchors (own work -> own products -> systems others rely on -> organizational portfolio) and named work products; see datacraft_proficiency_anchors.csv.

element: v1 Datacraft definition ('making patterns visible and projecting futures')
rationale: Pattern-making and projection are exactly what AI now produces cheaply. The irreducible human data-craft contribution is warrant: producing evidence whose provenance, method, uncertainty and fitness for a decision the practitioner can show and answer for, including when machines did the computation. Redefine accordingly (see report section 3).

v1 has 79 DC-primary and 91 DC-secondary tags (170 of 222). Rule 3 was right: Domain 1 science knowledge competencies (e.g., 1.1.1 Ecosystem dynamics, 1.1.3 Succession) are DC primary although their irreducible content is disciplinary knowledge used by all three crafts. Keep Rule 3 and add the knowledge-vs-craft distinction below.

element: DC-primary tags on Domain 1 science-knowledge competencies (26 of 40)
rationale: Disciplinary knowledge (ecology, hydrology, climate science, genetics) is the substrate for field, data and state craft alike. Tagging it DC primary inflates data craft and hides its dependence on field and institutional practice. Propose that v2 distinguish knowledge areas from craft practices (craft tags apply to practices; knowledge areas list which crafts draw on them). Decision for CA/IA.

element: Secondary-FC liberal rule for DC-primary competencies
rationale: Carry and strengthen: for any DC competency that validates or applies models/AI describing ecological condition (DC-CAND-09, -10, -13), FC secondary should be required, because out-of-distribution failures are recognized in the field first.

element: 3.4.3 Cryptocurrency, digital payments, and decentralized finance
rationale: Tool- and trend-bound; zero blockchain, cryptocurrency or distributed-ledger use cases among 438 USDA/DOI/EPA entries in the 2025 inventory; durable content (financial controls, donor transparency) is covered by 3.4.x and 6.6.x. Move blockchain/crypto to the tools layer as 'watch'.

Nearly every task specifies 'AI-powered', 'IoT', 'blockchain', 'RPA bots' or 'real-time dashboards'. This dates the competencies and makes them unassessable when tools change. Rewrite tasks by function (e.g., 'verify supply-chain material flows' not 'using blockchain and IoT'); move named technologies to the tools layer.

element: 6.7.2 T1 'Use environmental justice screening tools (EJSCREEN, CalEnviroScreen)'
rationale: Named public tools are volatile; my understanding is that EPA removed EJScreen from its website in early 2025 (expert recollection, not re-verified this session - LM/DB to confirm). Rewrite as 'apply cumulative-burden screening methods and evaluate the indicators and data behind them'; tools to tools layer.

element: 6.3.2 T2 'Use tools like InVEST or ARIES'
rationale: Tool names in task text; move to tools layer and state the durable method (ecosystem-service production-function modeling and validation).

element: 6.4.4 Public comment management (T2 classified S - substitution)
rationale: Deployed and piloted comment tools are documented as supplemental with analyst verification (FWS DocketScope; EPA Region 8 pilot; USDA pilot) and DOI's PCAT was retired between inventories (DC-001). Current evidence supports Ac/V (compressed, supervised), not S. LM owns exposure coding; DC recommends re-coding and linking to DC-CAND-16.

No USDA/DOI/EPA use case in the 2025 inventory reports AI as the principal basis for policy comparison or compliance determinations: EPA's high-impact cases prioritize inspections or pre-review documents, and the USDA permitting tool is explicitly 'recommendations for authorized staff to review'. S calls need direct evidence (LM lane).
